Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Efficient Data Labeling by Hierarchical Crowdsourcing with Large Language Models (ACL-Anthology-2025.coling-main.748-captured-copy) · paper method: The tariff comparison counts API or annotation charges while excluding model selection, GPT-4 prompt selection and worker-selection overhead; manual comparators use three university and six graduate students, so its cost curves do not establish end-to-end operating cost for an arbitrary workforce.

cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary

  • The historical tariff assumptions are not current price verification; no locally deployed-model compute cost parity is inferred.

Efficient Data Labeling by Hierarchical Crowdsourcing with Large Language Models (ACL-Anthology-2025.coling-main.748-captured-copy) · paper method: The authors limit their experiments to RTE, BoolQ and COPA and a restricted set of generic language models, identifying wider domains, datasets and model choices as future evaluation rather than demonstrated transfer.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Efficient Data Labeling by Hierarchical Crowdsourcing with Large Language Models (ACL-Anthology-2025.coling-main.748-captured-copy) · paper method: LMCrowd first aggregates labels from Llama2-7B, FLAN-T5-base, Zephyr-7B and Qwen-7B, then purchases GPT-4 relabeling to update uncertain label distributions; the evaluated models use four-shot prompts and paid-model responses remain uncertain rather than unquestioned truth.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Efficient Data Labeling by Hierarchical Crowdsourcing with Large Language Models (ACL-Anthology-2025.coling-main.748-captured-copy) · paper method: The main experiments compare annotation accuracy as a function of budget on RTE, BoolQ (a sampled 1.5K cases) and COPA, using majority-vote aggregation, approximate query selection and two relabeled tasks per iteration; the text describes the reported results as maximum achieved accuracy across configurations, not repeated-trial averages.
